title: Chitty Chitty Bang Bang
tagline: Wings out, napkins on. The schnitzel lands first.
about: An eccentric inventor rebuilds an old racing car for his two children, and it carries them, their father and a new friend to a kingdom where children are forbidden.
cue: Serve the snacks when Caractacus switches on his breakfast machine and it starts cooking on its own.
faces: England to Vulgaria. Wings out over the cliffs.
Pack the eggs, the sandwiches and a spare pair of goggles. I am not landing in a foreign country without my dinner.

    StartersBreakfast machine Scotch eggsSoft-centred boiled eggs wrapped in parsley and mustard sausage meat, crumbed and fried golden, with English mustardHow to make it5 eggs, 4 for boiling and 1 beaten400g pork sausage mince2 tbsp parsley, chopped1 tsp mustard powderblack pepper, to taste50g plain flour80g dry breadcrumbs1 L vegetable oil, for frying4 tbsp English mustard, to serveLower 4 eggs into boiling water for 6 1/2 minutes, then cool in iced water and peel.Mix the sausage mince with the parsley, mustard powder and pepper, divide into 4 and flatten each into a patty on wet hands.Wrap a patty around each egg, sealing it well.Roll in the flour, then the beaten egg, then the breadcrumbs.Chill for 20 minutes so they hold their shape. Heat the oil in a deep pan to 170°C.Fry 2 at a time, turning, until deep golden and cooked through, about 7 minutes.Drain, halve and serve warm with the mustard.Seaside picnic cucumber sandwichesCrustless white bread fingers with thin salted cucumber and lemon and dill cream cheeseHow to make it1 telegraph cucumber, very thinly sliced1/2 tsp salt125g cream cheese, softened40g butter, softened1 tbsp dill, chopped1 lemon, zestedwhite pepper, to taste8 slices of white breadToss the cucumber with the salt in a colander and leave to drain.Beat the cream cheese, butter, dill, lemon zest and a little white pepper until smooth.Spread over the bread, pat the cucumber dry and layer it over 4 slices, then close the sandwiches.Cut off the crusts and cut each sandwich into 3 fingers.Potted shrimp on hot toastPacked by Truly Scrumptious in the picnic hamper.How to make itA house standard, not part of tonight's cook.MainsBaron Bomburst's Vulgarian schnitzelThin crumbed pork schnitzel fried golden in butter, with lemon and a warm mustard and chive potato saladHow to make it800g kipfler potatoes1 small red onion, finely chopped125ml vegetable stock2 tbsp white wine vinegar1 tsp Dijon mustard3 tbsp vegetable oil, for the potatoes2 tbsp chives, choppedsalt and pepper, to taste600g pork loin steaks75g plain flour2 eggs, beaten150g dry breadcrumbs150ml vegetable oil, for frying30g butter2 lemons, in wedgesBoil the potatoes in salted water until tender.Warm the stock with the vinegar, mustard and onion. Slice the potatoes while hot, pour the dressing over, add the oil and chives, season and leave to soak.Pound the pork between sheets of baking paper to 5mm thin and season.Dip each in flour, then egg, then breadcrumbs, pressing them on.Fry in the oil and butter over medium high heat, 2 to 3 minutes a side, in batches, until golden and crisp.Serve with lemon wedges and the warm potato salad.Lord Scrumptious's roast beef and YorkshiresTruly's father, the sweet factory lord who won't buy the Toot SweetsHow to make it1.2kg beef sirloin roast3 tbsp vegetable oil1kg roasting potatoes140g plain flour3 eggs200ml milk400ml beef stock2 tbsp horseradish cream100ml thickened creamWhisk 120g of the flour, the eggs, milk and a pinch of salt into a smooth batter and leave to stand.Heat the oven to 220°C. Rub the beef with 1 tbsp of the oil and salt and roast for 45 minutes for medium rare, with the parboiled potatoes in 1 tbsp of oil on another tray.Rest the beef. Turn the oven to 230°C, put a drop of the rest of the oil in a 12-hole muffin tin and heat for 5 minutes, fill with batter and bake for 18 minutes until puffed.Stir the rest of the flour into the beef pan, whisk in the stock and simmer for 4 minutes for gravy. Whip the cream softly and fold in the horseradish.Carve and serve with the Yorkshires, potatoes, gravy and horseradish cream.SweetsToymaker's sticky gingerbread with custardDark, sticky golden syrup gingerbread with ginger and cinnamon, cut in warm squares under hot vanilla custardHow to make it125g butter125g brown sugar175g golden syrup250g plain flour2 tsp ground ginger1 tsp ground cinnamon1 tsp bicarbonate of soda1 egg200ml milk500ml vanilla custardHeat the oven to 170°C and line a 20cm square tin.Melt the butter, brown sugar and golden syrup together over low heat.Mix the flour, ginger, cinnamon and bicarbonate of soda, then whisk in the syrup mixture, the egg and the milk to a smooth batter.Pour into the tin and bake until risen and springy.Warm the custard in a small pan.Cut the gingerbread into squares and serve warm with the hot custard.DrinksJeremy and Jemima's lemon barley waterOld-fashioned cloudy barley water with lemon zest and juice, lightly sweet and served icy with lemon slicesHow to make it100g pearl barley1.5 L water3 lemons, zested and juiced100g caster sugar1 lemon, sliced, to serve4 cups iceRinse the barley, then simmer it with the water and lemon zest for 30 minutes.Strain into a jug over the sugar and stir until it dissolves.Cool, then chill until cold.Stir in the lemon juice and serve over ice with lemon slices.
